official.description: The Radboud Scholarship Programme is a partial scholarship for talented non-EU/EEA students pursuing a Master's at Radboud University in Nijmegen, funded by the Profiling Fund. It reduces the tuition fee to EUR 2,771 per academic year, covers the visa application fee, residence permit and Aon Student Insurance, and explicitly does not cover living and studying costs. A maximum of 26 scholarships are available for 2027-2028 spread across six faculties.
official.program_type: University partial tuition scholarship for master's students
official.english_requirement: You must meet the English language proficiency requirement of the Master's programme of your choice; the page recommends arranging a language test or exemption before 14 February 2027.

applicant_utility.summary: The Radboud Scholarship does not pay you money, it lowers your tuition to EUR 2,771 a year, so plan around what you owe rather than what you receive, and note the university itself flags that figure as to be confirmed. What the award really adds is the visa application fee, residence permit and the Aon Student Insurance health and liability policy, which are genuinely useful for an international applicant. The university is equally clear that living and studying costs in the Netherlands are not covered, and there are only 26 scholarships across six faculties for 2027-2028, so treat this as one of several funding sources rather than a full ride, and remember the NL Scholarship of EUR 5,000 stacks with it.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU master's applicants to a Radboud programme in a participating faculty who can cover Dutch living costs themselves and who want the fee reduction plus visa and insurance cover.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your master's is in one of the six faculties holding Radboud Scholarships and is not an Erasmus Mundus, dual or joint-degree programme
Prepare for both deadlines: OSIRIS submission by 31 January, 23:59 CET and a complete file by 14 February, 23:59 CET
Identify two referees early and make sure both upload their letters in OSIRIS before the deadline, since the references are a stated selection criterion
Arrange the language test or an exemption for your programme's English requirement well before 14 February
Budget around EUR 2,771 in fees plus rent, food and insurance in Nijmegen, since living costs are excluded
Apply for the NL Scholarship as well, since the two awards can be combined
common_rejection_risks: Assuming an incomplete application can be topped up after 14 February, when incomplete applications are not considered
Applying for an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree master's, which are excluded
Having only one reference letter uploaded by the deadline
Expecting the award to pay living costs in the Netherlands
Relying on a second year of the award without passing all first-year courses
